name: CPU cost of function-unit CodeRankEmbed embeddings
question: Can product search embed function units with nomic-ai/CodeRankEmbed on a CPU, as an opt-in mode, at an acceptable index time, query time and memory?
units: Product discovery (CodebaseContextManager.discover_files) and product parse_file: every top-level function and every class method, all parsed languages, test files included and counted separately. Text: relative path, newline, source lines of the unit.
config_meaning: weights - max tokens per unit - CPU threads. Each config runs in its own process, pinned with taskset to that many vCPUs; torch and OpenMP use the same thread count. The GPU is not used.

measure.sample: 1,000 units per repo (all units if fewer), random.Random(0); seconds per unit times the unit count gives the full index time
measure.check: one full index of cli/cli with fp32-512-8; it must fall within 20 percent of its estimate, else every estimate is reported as unreliable
measure.query: 50 workflow-pack query texts with the query prefix, one at a time, after 5 warm-up calls; p50 and p95
measure.memory: peak RSS of each config process
measure.int8: cosine of each int8 sample vector to its fp32 vector

rule.pass: At least one config with 8 threads meets all of: query p95 <= 150 ms; estimated full index <= 10 min for the median repo (by unit count) and <= 60 min for the largest; peak RSS <= 2 GiB. An int8 config counts only if its mean cosine to fp32 is >= 0.99.
rule.on_pass: Next step: an opt-in product mode and a quality test on Loc-Bench and fresh questions. A pass is not a quality result.
rule.on_fail: Report which limit fails and by how much. Do not tune the limits after the run.

limits: RunPod x86 server vCPUs (hyperthreads), not Apple Silicon. A Mac can use MPS, which is not measured here.
No retrieval quality is measured. The 0.739 Acc@5 of #241 used bf16, 1,024 tokens, Python-only CoRNStack units, on a GPU.
budget: RunPod $2 cap, one pod, destroyed by node name within 100 minutes of creation.
